title.narrative: Strengthening Commonwealth Member Countries to Access Climate Finance

description.narrative:
To advance equitable and inclusive climate action in small and other vulnerable Commonwealth states, through enhanced access to international climate finance and strengthened technical, human and institutional capacity.
Context and Need for the Project In no more than 200 words, provide the background and context to the issues this project will address and why the UK should fund this project
The Commonwealth Climate Change Programme focuses on strengthening the resilience of Commonwealth countries to the impacts of climate change. It provides technical assistance and capacity development support to member countries to access climate finance for climate mitigation and adaptation through the Commonwealth Climate Finance Access Hub (CCFAH). It supports integrated action on the three Rio Conventions through the implementation of the Living Lands Charter. As of March 2025, CCFAH has supported 21 countries in Africa, Indo-Pacific, and the Caribbean, securing approximately USD 473.55 million for various climate projects and training about 3,305 government officials through 152 capacity-building initiatives.
This funding from the FCDO, building on previous support including in FY24-25, will be used to cover the costs and expenses for Commonwealth National Climate Finance Adviser (CNCFA) in Maldives, Namibia and Mauritius, and the Commonwealth Regional Climate Finance Adviser (CRCFA) in the Caribbean region – nations and a region that are highly vulnerable to climate change.
The UK’s renewed commitment to climate leadership, exemplified by its ambitious 81% emissions reduction target by 2035, positions it as a trusted partner and climate leader, a reputation reinforced by this funding which will facilitate low-carbon transitions and de-risk investments in the long run. Strengthening climate adaptation in the Caribbean (a key Commonwealth trade partner) safeguards UK-linked industries like agriculture and tourism from climate disruptions.
